title: The bebop band at the Harlem Square
summary: Hitting on owner Joe for a job, he forms a bebop sextet with Blue Mitchell, Noel Cruz, Johnny Burdine and Abe Meeks, learning from records.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So I went down to the Harlem Square and hit on the man for a job. This guy was a Jew. His name was Joe--a little 'old short dude. Of course all Jews own--own the nightclubs down there. Really, actually. But his brother was the head of the liquor board, the State of Florida. So, let me make a long story short, the guy gave us--he say, well, I'll give you all a try, if you're, you know, if you're anything, you know--if you all make a, draw a crowd, make some people come in here and come in the lounge. Say, I'll give you all some more--I'll give you some more money, you know. If we make more money, you make more money. So, we don't have nothing to do--nothing to lose. So, so we all--five of us, man--but actually it was six of us--me; Mitchell Robinson, the drummer; Noel Cruz, the piano player, he was a fantastic piano player; and the drummer was....like, man--I ain't heard nobody yet like him; Blue Mitchell; Johnny Burdine, we was still together--me and this saxophone player, Johnny Burdine; and a trombone player named Abe Meeks--Abe Meeks. Our only repertory was nothing but be-bop.
So we play--we playing all the music we heard. We learn how to play from the records--all the Charlie Parker, all the Dizzy Gillespie's, all the Dexter
Gordon--anything you'd name. Lester--Johnny Burdine, he was a Lester Young man, you know.
So Abe Meeks, he got drafted in the Army. So that left the five of us. So, now we're really into very dizzying stuff, now.
